topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture's scope, connects it to prior practical histopathology work, and outlines the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and describe the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification of cancer genes and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated genes and illustrate how mutation types and allele dosage alter cell cycle control through pathways like Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, their underlying DNA repair and mitotic defects, and their cellular consequences.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary cancer syndromes, and tumor maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the stepwise progression of cancer mutations, how inherited predisposing mutations accelerate this pathway, and the role of genetic instability during tumor maintenance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This topic wraps up the lecture with concluding remarks, recommended reading material, and framing for the upcoming session.
